notes: THE READ, over all 1,255 wheel team-seasons that can field a five (scripts/tactics115.ts).
before  balanced 457 · fiveout 17 · pnr 224 · motion 5 · postup 341 · helio 203 · transition 8
after   balanced 439 · fiveout 17 · pnr 332 · motion 6 · postup 239 · helio 214 · transition 8
222 of 1,255 fives changed style; 64 of them post-up to pick-and-roll, 27 post-up to balanced,
15 post-up to helio, and 62 balanced to pick-and-roll.
HIS CASE. Jazz '97 post-up 81 (Malone) -> PICK-AND-ROLL 76 (Stockton + Malone). The post-up on
the same big now reads 69 and helio reads 72, so the pair wins the floor outright.
WHY IT WAS WRONG. Both two-man terms were MINIMA, and a minimum asks a man to be two things at
once. min(playvol, volume) read Stockton '97 (playvol 96, volume 23) as 23 and Nash '05 (97, 42)
as 42 — the measure said a pass-first point guard cannot run a pick-and-roll, which is the
opposite of true. min(rim, efficiency) read the ROLL only, so a screener who pops was paid
nothing for it and Malone '97 (rim 77, mid 94) read 77.
WHAT REPLACED THEM. handlerFit = 0.60 playvol + 0.24 volume + up to ELITE_LIFT 24 on a ramp from
ELITE_PV 80 to 95 — his words, "playvol in the ~90s" — clamped to 99. screenFit = min(max(rim,
mid), efficiency), the best finish off the screen, roll or pop. And the mid-range MOVED rather
than being invented twice: recal_115 had put max(rim, mid) into the post-up hub, and a big who
scores from the elbow is being screened free by a guard, not fed on the block, so the hub goes
back to min(rim, volume) x interior. Neither half reaches the ruling alone — the handler term
alone leaves Jazz '97 at pnr 70 against post-up 81.
WHY THE RAMP IS NARROW. Measured at 78-to-90 instead of 80-to-95, the elite ramp also lifts
Muggsy Bogues (playvol 92) far enough to take Alonzo Mourning's Hornets '95 off the post — one
of the four hub families the ruling protects. The narrow ramp holds all 23 of the protected
post-up fives and all seven of the protected pick-and-rolls. Its one cost is recorded: Stockton
'99, whose playvol fell to 86, is the only Stockton/Malone year that does not read pick-and-roll
(pnr 69.1, helio 69.4 — a quarter of a point), and widening the ramp to catch it is not worth a
protected hub.
THE WEIGHTS WERE NOT TOUCHED. Moving the three pnr shares toward the pair (0.44/0.36/0.20) was
measured first: it reaches the ruling too, but it costs the well-spaced pick-and-roll fives
their read — Nuggets '25 (Murray + Jokic) and Thunder '25 (Gilgeous-Alexander + Hartenstein)
both fall to helio. The ruling names the two terms, not their shares, so the shares stand.
WHAT ELSE CAME WITH IT, and it is the argument for the round. Every Stockton/Malone Jazz year
except '99 now reads the pick-and-roll; so do Hardaway + Mourning ('97, '98), Mark Jackson +
Ewing ('88, '89), Nash + Nowitzki ('02, '04), Jason Williams + Gasol ('03), Van Exel + McDyess
('00, '01), Strickland + Webber ('98) and Parker + Duncan ('12). Those are the canonical
pick-and-roll teams of their eras and every one of them was reading post-up.
WHAT IT COST. LaMarcus Aldridge's fives lose the post: Spurs '17 (post-up 82) and '16, Blazers
'10 and '15 now read helio on Leonard, Roy and Lillard — no man on those fives clears the
handler gate, so the pick-and-roll cannot pick them up. Kevin Garnett's Timberwolves ('00, '03,
'06, '07) go the same way, which is arguably a better read of a five that was one man. Late
Olajuwon ('98, '99) and late Duncan ('15) fall to balanced.
OPEN. The handler gate is still playvol >= 70 AND height <= 78, recal_58's, and it is what
leaves Spurs '17 and Blazers '15 with no handler at all. A six-foot-nine primary creator
(Doncic '26, James '16) can never be read as one. That is the next thing to look at in this
file, and it is not this round's ruling.
